title: Miniature HVAC Airflow Particle Visualization Diorama
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D miniature diorama of a building cross-section showing HVAC airflow using particle systems in Three.js.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a perspective camera at position (8, 6, 8) looking at origin
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8
- Create a cutaway diorama of a 2-story building (approx 6x4x6 units) with visible rooms:
  - Ground floor: living room (left) and kitchen (right)
  - Upper floor: bedroom (left) and bathroom (right)
  - A central vertical duct connecting floors (width 0.4 units)
  - Horizontal ducts along ceilings of each room (height 0.3 units)
- Render walls as semi-transparent (opacity 0.3) so particles are visible inside
- Add colored floor planes: living room (beige), kitchen (light gray), bedroom (light blue), bathroom (white)
- Place a visible HVAC unit (box 0.8x0.8x0.8) on the roof, colored dark gray

PARTICLE SYSTEM:
- Implement a particle system with exactly 500 particles representing airflow
- Particles spawn from the HVAC unit on the roof and flow down through the central duct
- At each floor, particles branch into horizontal ducts and disperse into rooms through vents
- Particle color encodes temperature: blue (cold, 16°C) -> green (20°C) -> red (hot, 28°C)
- Particles have velocity vectors influenced by duct geometry and room boundaries
- Particles that reach room boundaries recirculate back toward return vents
- Each particle has: position (vec3), velocity (vec3), temperature (float), age (float), room (string)
- Particle max age is 8 seconds; particles respawn at HVAC unit when expired

PHYSICS CONSTRAINTS:
- Airflow speed in ducts: 2.0 units/sec (±0.2 tolerance)
- Airflow speed in rooms: 0.5 units/sec (±0.1 tolerance)
- Temperature decreases by 0.5°C per second as air travels from HVAC (cooling mode)
- Temperature increases by 0.5°C per second in heating mode
- Total particle count must remain exactly 500 (conservation)
- Particles must stay within building bounds (no escaping geometry)

USER INTERACTIONS:
- OrbitControls for camera rotation
- Keyboard 'H' toggles heating mode (target 26°C) vs cooling mode (target 18°C)
- Keyboard 'P' pauses/resumes particle simulation
- Keyboard '1','2','3','4' selects individual rooms (1=living, 2=kitchen, 3=bedroom, 4=bathroom) highlighting that room
- Keyboard '0' deselects all rooms
- Keyboard 'F' toggles fan speed: low (0.5x velocity multiplier), medium (1.0x), high (1.5x)
- Click on the HVAC unit mesh to toggle system on/off
- DOM button 'Reset' resets all particles to initial state at HVAC unit
- DOM slider (id='tempSlider', range 16-28, step 0.5) sets target temperature
- Keyboard 'U' performs undo on the last mode change (heating/cooling toggle)

HUD/UI:
- Top-left overlay (id='hud') showing: mode (heating/cooling), fan speed, system on/off, selected room, target temp, average particle temp
- DOM button with id='resetBtn'
- DOM slider with id='tempSlider'
- Display particle count and average temperature in HUD

STATE MANAGEMENT - expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- mode: 'cooling' | 'heating'
- previousMode: 'cooling' | 'heating' | null (for undo)
- fanSpeed: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'
- fanMultiplier: 0.5 | 1.0 | 1.5
- systemOn: boolean
- paused: boolean
- selectedRoom: null | 'living' | 'kitchen' | 'bedroom' | 'bathroom'
- targetTemp: number
- particleCount: number (must always be 500)
- avgTemp: number (average temperature of all particles)
- particlesInBounds: number (count of particles within building geometry)
- roomParticleCounts: {living: n, kitchen: n, bedroom: n, bathroom: n, duct: n}
- elapsedTime: number (simulation seconds)
- ductSpeed: number (measured average speed in ducts)
- roomSpeed: number (measured average speed in rooms)
- undoStack: array of previous states
- lastAction: string describing last user action
physics_constraints: Particle count conservation: always exactly 500 particles. Duct airflow speed 2.0 ±0.2 units/sec. Room airflow speed 0.5 ±0.1 units/sec. Temperature delta rate 0.5°C/sec. All particles must remain within building bounds (particlesInBounds === 500). Temperature range clamped to [16, 28]°C.
